Telsiai Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Telšių apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Telšiai — known as Telz in Yiddish — became a center of Torah learning for the entire Jewish world thanks to the Telz Yeshiva; though the yeshiva was closed after the 1940 Soviet occupation, its name and teaching methods traveled to the United States, where the Telshe Yeshiva tradition continues today. The town's Soldiers' Beit Midrash and Tailors' Beit Midrash both still stand, preserving distinctive Litvak synagogue architecture. Under Lithuanian independence, Telšiai was home to the only Jewish teachers' seminary in the country, part of the 'Yavneh' network; an earlier attempt to establish a leftist Hebrew school had failed there fifty years before, just as one directed by the celebrated Haskalah poet Judah Leib Gordon had also failed. The entire Jewish community was killed piecemeal between June 26 and December 25, 1941, across at least four massacre sites, the largest at Rainiai forest. This cemetery has shrunk drastically from its original 2.17 hectares to just 0.43, after the largest part was destroyed as late as 1987 — one of the latest Soviet-era cemetery demolitions recorded in this collection — and replaced by a park. A 2018 restoration project cleaned and translated about 200 surviving monuments, including the grave of Rabbi Yosef Leib Bloch, head of the Telz Yeshiva.
